summary: K. V. Raman specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras (~1954–1956), and the Institute of Archaeology, later holding posts at Madras and the Archaeological Survey of India.

K. V. Ramesh was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987) and as Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang at Peking University (1947–1949), Prabodh Chandra Bagchi (1950), and at Visva-Bharati University, where he also taught, and visited Harvard-Yenching Institute.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Kaie Mochizuki is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. His academic career includes serving as professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and university president (学長, attested 2026) at Minobusan University.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyo Mitomo. He held a position as assistant professor (助教授) at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaigyoku Watanabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He served as principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School and held professorships at Taisho, Toyo, and Kokushikan universities.

Kaiten Nukariya specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Komazawa University, Keio University, and other schools, later serving as head teacher and the first president of Komazawa University, as well as lecturing at Harvard University.
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as professor (attested 1999–2002).

Kakichi Kadowaki was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1944–1947) and under Sogen Omori, and later served on the faculty at Sophia University (~1970–1997).

Kalidas Nag was an Indologist and historian who studied at Scottish Church College (~1908–1912) and the University of Calcutta (~1912–1914). He later held posts at Scottish Church College (~1915–1919) and the University of Calcutta (~1923–1955).

Kalu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Palpung Monastery under Drupon Norbu Dondrup and others, served as Palpung's Vajra Master (~1939–1955), and was abbot of Changchub Chöling Monastery (1957).

Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology and Sinology who studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served at the University of Windsor, where he held the rank of Professor Emeritus (attested 2002).
Kamal K. Sridhar is an Indologist and linguist. She held positions at Stony Brook University, serving as director (attested 2007) and Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there (1993–1994).

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. Over the course of his career, he held academic appointments at the University of Bonn, the University of Toronto (~1969–1971), and Brown University (~1971–1974).

Kamil Václav Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD from Charles University. He held positions at the Oriental Institute (ASCR), Charles University, and later served as professor of Dravidian linguistics and literature at Utrecht University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi, an Indologist, studied under Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidas Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor to the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (attested 2009).

Kammie Morrison Takahashi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia (PhD 2009) under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama.
Kan Hang is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Bai Su. He has served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.
